summary-text: Acceleration phase (~47%): the shock is deepening, not resolving. Hormuz disruption → Energy cost advantage shifts to China → Trade surplus swells → Capital controls retain surplus → RMB appreciates → Central banks diversify → Dollar share erodes → Multi-polar system emerges. THIS WEEK (Sep 7-13): A ONE-CHOKEPOINT PROBLEM BECAME A TWO-CHOKEPOINT PROBLEM. Hormuz transits fell BACK to 7 on Sep 9 from 12 the previous day (10-day avg 14) — still ~83% below the pre-war ~138/day. The 'tanker-for-tanker' spiral escalated: CENTCOM disabled 5 Iranian tankers (Kaviz, Charminar, Horizon 1, Risco, Darya) on Sep 8; the IRGC claimed strikes on 2 US destroyers + 18 vessels on Sep 9 and fired 20 ballistic missiles at Al Azraq in Jordan (18 intercepted). The US Navy's Bahrain hub is OUT OF ACTION — the Acting Navy Secretary admitted the 5th Fleet HQ cannot support USS Abraham Lincoln operations and Adm. Caudle says the service will not return 'anytime soon'. Saudi Arabia SHUT its East-West pipeline (4-5 mb/d = 4-5% of global supply) on Sep 10 after drone strikes launched from Iraq; the Houthis seized Mokha and Perim island and now control Bab el-Mandeb. Kpler: Saudi exports to Asia fell from ~3.4 mb/d (Jun) to 128K bpd (Aug), recovering to ~700K. MBS called Trump at least twice on Sep 10 for military help; Washington declined direct action (intelligence/targeting only). Brent settled above $100 on Sep 9 ($101.21, first triple-digit close since July) and ended the week at $104.61 (+9% w/w, +56% YoY); per-ship transit costs are $10-20M with some vessels now sailing uninsured. GCC foreign ministers meet Iran in Oman on Monday Sep 14 over a temporary shipping arrangement — the first real off-ramp test. CHINA: August trade surplus hit a RECORD $119.09B (exports +25% to $401.44B; to the US +34.4%); Jan-Aug vehicle exports 7.15M incl. 3.44M NEVs (+124%) — China exported more cars in eight months than in all of 2025; DeepSeek shipped V4.1-Flash on Sep 10; the PBoC added 650K oz of gold in August (22nd straight month, largest since Oct 2023) with FX reserves at $3.4383T; CFETS 101.64 (Sep 4, −0.23 w/w), USD/CNY 6.7075 (Sep 11, +5.82% YoY). THE STRUCTURAL REVEAL OF THE WEEK: Pew's Spring 2026 survey shows China now viewed more favourably than the US in 25 of 36 countries — China median 51% vs US 37%, the first inversion of the series — with a median 75% saying the US interferes in others' affairs vs 45% for China.
